forwarding.checkIt: To check it works, send an email to {{email}} from another account. It shows up as a new ticket in Unassigned.

gmail.s1: In Gmail, open Settings, then See all settings, then Forwarding and POP/IMAP.
gmail.s2: Choose Add a forwarding address and paste the address above.
gmail.s3: Gmail sends a confirmation email. It arrives in opendesk as a ticket: open it and click the link, or copy the code into Gmail.
gmail.s4: Back in Gmail, select Forward a copy of incoming mail to the new address and save.

workspace.s1: For one mailbox, follow the Gmail steps while signed in as that user.
workspace.s2: For a group or many users, open the Google Admin console, then Apps, Google Workspace, Gmail, Routing.
workspace.s3: Add a routing rule for the address, choose Also deliver to and add the address above as a recipient.
workspace.s4: Save. Changes can take a few minutes to apply.

microsoft.s1: Open the Exchange admin center, then Recipients, Mailboxes, and select the mailbox.
microsoft.s2: Under Mail flow settings, choose Manage email forwarding.
microsoft.s3: Turn on forwarding, paste the address above, and keep Deliver to both on if the mailbox should still get a copy.
microsoft.s4: If outbound forwarding is blocked, allow it in the outbound spam policy, or use an Outlook rule that forwards to the address instead.

gmail.banner: An app password connects Gmail or Google Workspace over IMAP and SMTP in about two minutes.
gmail.s1Sub: Google only offers app passwords on accounts that have it on.
gmail.s1a: Open your Google Account's security page and find 2-Step Verification under How you sign in to Google.
gmail.s1b: Turn it on with a phone prompt, an authenticator app or a text message.
gmail.s1Note: On Google Workspace an admin can require or block 2-Step Verification for the organization. Accounts in Advanced Protection can't have app passwords.
gmail.s2Sub: A 16-letter password Google makes for one app. opendesk stores it encrypted.
gmail.s2a: Open the app passwords page. Google may ask you to sign in again.
gmail.s2b: Type opendesk as the app name and choose Create.
gmail.s2c: Copy the 16 letters it shows. The spaces don't matter.
gmail.s2Note: No app passwords page? 2-Step Verification is still off, or your Google Workspace admin has turned app passwords off for your organization. Ask them to allow app passwords for your account.
gmail.s3Sub: Paste the app password. Nothing else to type.
gmail.lengthHint: Google app passwords are 16 letters. This looks like something else, maybe the account password. It's checked when you connect either way.
gmail.s3Note: Use the address you sign in to Google with, not an alias. Deleting the app password in your Google Account disconnects the mailbox.

yahoo.s1: Sign in to Yahoo and open Account security.
yahoo.s2: Choose Generate app password, name it opendesk and choose Generate password.
yahoo.s3: Copy the password and paste it below.

aol.s1: Sign in to AOL and open Account security.
aol.s2: Choose Generate app password, name it opendesk and choose Generate password.
aol.s3: Copy the password and paste it below.

icloud.s1: Sign in at account.apple.com and open Sign-In and Security. Two-factor authentication must be on.
icloud.s2: Choose App-Specific Passwords and add one named opendesk.
icloud.s3: Copy the password and paste it below. The address must be your iCloud address, not an alias.

fastmail.s1: In Fastmail open Settings, Privacy and Security, then Manage app passwords.
fastmail.s2: Create one named opendesk with access to IMAP and SMTP.
fastmail.s3: Copy the password and paste it below.

zoho.s1: In Zoho Accounts open Security, then App Passwords.
zoho.s3: Copy it and paste it below. Also check that IMAP access is on in Zoho Mail settings under Mail Accounts.

yandex.s1: Open Yandex ID, then Security and App passwords.
yandex.s3: Copy it and paste it below. Also allow IMAP in Yandex Mail settings under Email clients.

connect.forwardingIntro: After you create it, you get a private address to forward this mailbox's mail to. Nothing is shared but the mail you forward.
